name: ChatRoom - multi-user TCP chat with threads

steps.content:
import socket
import time
import unittest

from chat.client import ChatClient
from chat.protocol import decode, encode
from chat.server import ChatServer


def wait_until(check, timeout=2.0):
    end = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < end:
        if check():
            return True
        time.sleep(0.02)
    return False


class ServerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.server = ChatServer()
        self.host, self.port = self.server.start()
        self.clients = []

    def tearDown(self):
        for client in self.clients:
            client.quit()
        self.server.stop()

    def connect(self, nick):
        client = ChatClient(self.host, self.port, nick)
        self.clients.append(client)
        return client

    def test_welcome_registers_nickname(self):
        ana = self.connect("ana")
        self.assertEqual(ana.wait_for("welcome")["nick"], "ana")
        self.assertTrue(wait_until(lambda: self.server.nicknames() == ["ana"]))

    def test_message_reaches_everyone(self):
        ana, ben = self.connect("ana"), self.connect("ben")
        ana.wait_for("welcome")
        ben.wait_for("welcome")
        ana.say("hello")
        for client in (ana, ben):
            msg = client.wait_for("say")
            self.assertEqual((msg["nick"], msg["text"]), ("ana", "hello"))

    def test_duplicate_nick_rejected(self):
        self.connect("ana").wait_for("welcome")
        twin = self.connect("ana")
        self.assertEqual(twin.wait_for("error")["text"], "nickname unavailable")

    def test_must_join_first(self):
        raw = socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port))
        raw.sendall(encode("say", text="hi"))
        reply = decode(raw.makefile("rb").readline())
        self.assertEqual(reply["text"], "join first")
        raw.close()

    def test_who_lists_everyone(self):
        ana, ben = self.connect("ana"), self.connect("ben")
        ana.wait_for("welcome")
        ben.wait_for("welcome")
        wait_until(lambda: len(self.server.nicknames()) == 2)
        ana.who()
        self.assertEqual(ana.wait_for("who")["nicks"], ["ana", "ben"])

    def test_leaving_removes_nickname(self):
        ana, ben = self.connect("ana"), self.connect("ben")
        ana.wait_for("welcome")
        ben.wait_for("welcome")
        ben.quit()
        self.assertTrue(wait_until(lambda: self.server.nicknames() == ["ana"]))

    def test_long_messages_are_trimmed(self):
        ana = self.connect("ana")
        ana.wait_for("welcome")
        ana.say("x" * 2000)
        self.assertEqual(len(ana.wait_for("say")["text"]), 500)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from chat.client import ChatClient
from chat.server import ChatServer


def show(who, msg):
    if msg["type"] == "say":
        print(f"[{who} sees] <{msg['nick']}> {msg['text']}")
    elif msg["type"] == "who":
        print(f"[{who} sees] online: {', '.join(msg['nicks'])}")
    elif msg["type"] == "notice":
        print(f"[{who} sees] * {msg['text']}")


def drain(who, client):
    while True:
        msg = client.next_message(timeout=0.4)
        if msg is None:
            return
        show(who, msg)


def main():
    server = ChatServer()
    host, port = server.start()
    print(f"server listening on {host}:{port}")
    ana = ChatClient(host, port, "ana")
    ana.wait_for("welcome")
    ben = ChatClient(host, port, "ben")
    ben.wait_for("welcome")
    ana.say("hi ben!")
    ben.say("hey ana, this is running over real sockets")
    ana.who()
    drain("ana", ana)
    drain("ben", ben)
    ben.quit()
    ana.quit()
    server.stop()
    print("done")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Chat room

A small multi-user chat over TCP sockets, one JSON message per line.

    python demo.py                      # server + two clients in one script
    python -m chat serve --port 9000    # terminal 1
    python -m chat join ana --port 9000 # terminal 2 (/who, /quit)
    python -m unittest -v
